title: How to prevent business identity fraud in account opening
summary: Explore risk-based defense frameworks to mitigate business identity fraud during commercial account opening, from automated KYB to verified tax checks.
body_markdown:
When applicants submit corporate documentation through automated onboarding funnels, underwriters must verify information across independent government and postal databases. Institutions reduce commercial onboarding risk by establishing four automated verification controls at intake:


State corporate charter verification: Querying state Secretary of State corporate databases confirms active legal standing, entity structure, formation date, and historical filings. Reviewing filing histories surfaces sudden, recent alterations in corporate officers or registered agents that often signal corporate identity takeover.


Federal tax identifier matching: Eligible payers and their authorized agents can use IRS TIN Matching for information reporting to check whether a submitted payee name and TIN match IRS records.


Postal delivery point classification: Assessing physical operating addresses using the USPS Delivery Point Validation (DPV) system confirms address deliverability and identifies Commercial Mail Receiving Agency (CMRA) indicators and private mailboxes.


Beneficial ownership and signer authorization: Where the federal beneficial ownership rule applies, a covered institution identifies and verifies the identity of each individual who owns 25% or more of the entity, directly or indirectly, and one individual with significant responsibility to control, manage, or direct it.
